howItWorks.title: How it works
howItWorks.intro: ResearchHub guides a scientific project from draft proposal to completed campaign. Status transitions are enforced on the server — you cannot skip steps.

phases.title: Before acceptance
phases.body: While the project is a draft (and later under review), you prepare the science case: objectives, proposal text, planned experiments, existing related publications, and your team.

phases.title: After acceptance
phases.body: Once an admin approves the proposal, you schedule and run executed experiments. The first executed experiment moves the project to in progress. Then you can add resulting publications and finally mark the project complete.

steps.title: Create and prepare
steps.body: Create a project with title, description, and scientific objective. In draft you can write the proposal, invite collaborators, add planned experiments (intent for the campaign), and link existing or related publications.
items: Proposal methodology and expected results
Planned experiments only
Existing / related publications only
Invite editors and viewers by email

steps.title: Submit for scientific review
steps.body: When the proposal is ready, an owner or editor submits it. The project enters review. Platform admins see it in the separate admin application and approve or reject it.
items: Researchers cannot approve their own proposals
Review happens in the admin app, not client-ui
Invalid status jumps are blocked by the API

steps.title: Start executed work
steps.body: After approval you may add executed experiments (schedule / run). Planned experiments stay as proposal artifacts and are no longer editable. Resulting publications are not available yet until work has started.
items: Add executed experiments
First executed experiment → project becomes IN_PROGRESS

steps.title: Run the campaign
steps.body: Continue executed experiments and record resulting publications that come from this project's work. Owners and editors can mark the project complete when the campaign is finished.
items: Executed experiments
Resulting publications
Complete action available to editors

steps.title: Close the project
steps.body: The project is closed. You can still attach resulting publications. Rejected proposals stop the lifecycle; they do not move to experiments.
items: Resulting publications still allowed
REJECTED ends the path — no executed work

roles.title: Owner
roles.body: Creates the project, invites collaborators, can delete the project, and has full edit rights.

roles.title: Editor
roles.body: Can edit proposal, experiments, and publications according to project status; can submit the proposal and complete the project.

roles.title: Viewer
roles.body: Read-only access to the project and its sections.

roles.title: Platform admin
roles.body: Uses the admin app to review proposals and manage platform users. Super admins alone can create other admins.

documentation.title: Documentation
documentation.intro: Practical guide to ResearchHub for researchers. This matches what the product does today — not future features.

sections.title: Accounts & login
sections.body: Register with email and password as a researcher. Log in from client-ui. Sessions use JWT access and refresh tokens stored only for this browser origin.
items: One account email per invitation accept
Admin staff use a separate admin application and origin

sections.title: Projects
sections.body: A research project holds overview metadata, team, proposal, experiments, and publications. Open a project to see Overview always on top, then switch sections with tabs: Team, Proposal, Experiments, Publications.
items: Statuses: DRAFT → SUBMITTED → UNDER_REVIEW → APPROVED → IN_PROGRESS → COMPLETED (or REJECTED)
Dashboard lists your projects and pending invitations

sections.title: Team & invitations
sections.body: Owners invite collaborators by email with role EDITOR or VIEWER. The invitee must sign in with the same email and accept under Invitations. Access is granted only after acceptance — never when the invite is merely created.
items: Invitations expire after 7 days
Owners can cancel pending invitations
Tokens are not exposed in normal project API responses

sections.title: Proposal
sections.body: Create methodology and expected results while the project is DRAFT. Submit for review when ready. Admins approve or reject from the admin app.
items: Only one proposal per project
Submit moves the project into the review path

sections.title: Experiments (planned vs executed)
sections.body: Experiments have a kind that follows the lifecycle.
items: PLANNED — proposal intent; create/edit only in DRAFT
EXECUTED — after acceptance; create/edit when APPROVED or IN_PROGRESS
First EXECUTED on an APPROVED project starts IN_PROGRESS
Each experiment also has a run status: planned, scheduled, completed, or cancelled

sections.title: Publications (existing vs resulting)
sections.body: Publications also have a kind tied to project status.
items: EXISTING — related or prior work cited in the proposal; DRAFT only
RESULTING — outputs of this campaign; IN_PROGRESS or COMPLETED
Cannot add resulting publications while still only APPROVED

sections.title: Admin review
sections.body: Platform admins work in admin-ui. They list pending proposals, approve or reject, view projects and related entities, and (as super admin) manage admin accounts separately from researchers.
items: Researchers never appear as creatable admins via role flip
Admin API calls require the admin origin

sections.title: What is not in the product yet
sections.body: These are planned later and are not available in the UI today.
items: Request changes / resubmit / closed statuses
Results entity and document uploads
Public project pages
Email notifications beyond invitation plumbing
